tests.name: pure function: missing pose gives zero Twist
pure function: regular pose gives linear.x=0.5, angular.z=0.3
pure function: command limits, integer inputs and non-finite values
node: relative cmd_vel resolves to /cmd_vel, remap gives /turtle1/cmd_vel, timer period 0.1 s
node: zero command until first pose, then 0.5/0.3
zero command on /cmd_vel before turtlesim publishes a pose
without remap: /cmd_vel has patrol publisher and no subscribers, turtle does not move
with remap: /turtle1/cmd_vel has patrol publisher and turtlesim subscriber, turtle moves
command rate on /turtle1/cmd_vel is about 10 Hz over a window longer than 10 s (logs/3-hz.txt)
after Ctrl+C the turtle keeps moving for less than 1 s until the turtlesim command timeout, then stops (logs/4-stop.txt)

defect.reproducer: ros2 run patrol patrol without remap: ros2 node info /patrol showed the publisher on /cmd_vel; ros2 topic info /cmd_vel --verbose showed Publisher count: 1 (patrol) and Subscription count: 0; ros2 topic info /turtle1/cmd_vel --verbose showed Publisher count: 0 and Subscription count: 1 (turtlesim); /turtle1/pose stayed at the spawn point x=y=5.5444, theta=0 while /cmd_vel carried linear.x=0.5, angular.z=0.3.
defect.root_cause: The node publishes to the relative name cmd_vel. In the root namespace it resolves to /cmd_vel, while turtlesim subscribes to /turtle1/cmd_vel. Discovery sees both endpoints, but they belong to different topics, so the command is never delivered even though the message type is the same.
defect.proof_after: Only the launch command changed: ros2 run patrol patrol --ros-args -r cmd_vel:=/turtle1/cmd_vel. ros2 topic info /turtle1/cmd_vel --verbose showed Publisher count: 1 (patrol) and Subscription count: 1 (turtlesim), /cmd_vel disappeared, the pose changed between two reads with linear_velocity=0.5, and ros2 topic hz /turtle1/cmd_vel measured about 10 Hz over a window longer than 10 s (logs/2-fixed.txt, logs/3-hz.txt).
